title: The bike computer that froze mid-ride
hints: Run it and open the Timeline. By tick 4, `nav` holds `gps_lock` and waits for `sd_lock`, while `archive` holds `sd_lock` and waits for `gps_lock`. Each waits for the other forever. Which of the four deadlock conditions is the easiest one to break here?

Break the circular wait. Pick one global order, gps before sd (nav already uses it), and make `archive` follow it too: take `gps_lock` first, then `sd_lock`, and release in reverse. Then no task can ever hold sd while waiting for gps.

In `archive_task`: `rtos_mutex_lock(gps_lock, RTOS_WAIT_FOREVER); rtos_mutex_lock(sd_lock, RTOS_WAIT_FOREVER); rtos_busy(2); archive_stamp(); rtos_mutex_unlock(sd_lock); rtos_mutex_unlock(gps_lock);`. Write the order in a comment next to the mutex declarations so the next person keeps it.
